issues.description: Conflicting specification for the SealSaloon.stock attribute. The problem statement first instructs that SealSaloon should have a final Stock field that is initialized to a default value in the SealSaloon constructor (problem_statement.md lines 70-71). Later the problem statement requires that the stock attribute must be static/shared across all instances (problem_statement.md lines 77-80). These two requirements conflict because a static field is not per-instance and cannot be meaningfully "initialized in the constructor" for each instance. The reference solution declares the field as a static final Stock and initializes it at declaration: "private static final Stock stock = new Stock();" (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java lines 4-6). This contradiction will confuse students whether to implement stock as an instance final field initialized in the constructor or as a static final field initialized at declaration/static initializer.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the contradiction by choosing one consistent design in the problem statement and tests: either (A) require an instance (non-static) final Stock and explicitly instruct students to initialize it in the SealSaloon constructor (and remove the statement that stock must be static), or (B) require a static final Stock shared across instances and instruct students to initialize it at the field declaration or in a static initializer (and remove the instruction to initialize it in the instance constructor). Update the problem text (problem_statement.md) and any tests to reflect the chosen design. If keeping the solution as-is, prefer option (B) and change the constructor-initialization sentence to state that stock should be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer.
